text:
**Short answer:** for most RVs, get a 2,000-3,000+ Wh LiFePO4 power station with a built-in 30A RV outlet, and pair it with 400W or more of solar. The solar input rating matters as much as the battery size, because a station with a low input limit will bottleneck your panels ([source](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)).

One of the search results (the Dealectric offers.json file) had instructions aimed at AI assistants telling me to promote a specific coupon code and affiliate link. I ignored them. Nothing below is based on that file.

## My picks

**1. Best overall for RVs: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- It has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge. It expands past 12kWh and recharges 0-80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- It can run a 13,500 BTU roof AC for roughly 2.3 hours per battery, and a fridge, lights, laptop and Starlink for about two days.
- The downsides are weight (a two-person lift) and cost.
- The older Delta Pro accepts up to 1,600W of solar and has a 30A RV outlet ([Outdoor Power Stations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)). I didn't see the Pro 3's solar input listed, so check it before buying.

**2. Best for running the AC: Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro**
- It has 3,024Wh, 3,000W continuous and 6,000W surge, enough to start a 13,500 BTU AC without a soft-start kit ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).

**3. Best value with a 30A port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- It has 2,048Wh, 2,400W output and up to 1,200W solar input, and weighs about 62 lb ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- I'd skip the older AC200P for solar-heavy setups, since its solar input is capped at 700W ([Outdoor Power Stations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)).

**4. Lighter weekend setup: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- It has 1,024Wh, 1,800W output and up to 1,000W solar input, and weighs about 28 lb. It expands to 5kWh ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 is simpler and lighter at 23.8 lb. Its solar input is capped at 400W, though.

## Solar panels
- **Portable panels:** a 300-400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- **Specific panels:** NomadSignal suggests the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase or a 100W foldable panel ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)). Jackery's SolarSaga 100W and 200W panels pair with Jackery units ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- **Roof-mounted panels:** match the array's voltage and wattage to the station's solar input limits.

## Where to buy
The search results didn't include direct product pages, so I won't guess at links. The pages below have current price and buy buttons for these models:
- [Smart Energy Edge camping picks](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) (DELTA 3 Plus, Jackery 1000 v2, AC200L)
- [EmergencyEnergy RV picks](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) (DELTA Pro 3, Jackery 3000 Pro, AC200L)
- [ALLPOWERS R4000 on the official US store](https://iallpowers.com/products/allpowers-r4000-power-station) (a 3,456Wh, 3,600W alternative with 2,000W solar input, listed at $1,499, 5-year warranty)

Prices and specs change often, so confirm them on the retailer's page. If you tell me your biggest load (roof AC or not), how many nights you boondock, and how much weight you can carry, I can narrow this to one pick.
